jobs.title: Distinguished Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Credit Acceptance is proud to be an award-winning company recognized both locally and nationally across multiple workplace categories.
jobs.description:
Credit Acceptance is proud to be an award-winning company recognized both locally and nationally across multiple workplace categories. Our world-class culture is shaped by dedicated team members who are driven to succeed as professionals individually and together as a team. Backed by a strong product, exceptional people, and a stable financial foundation, we’ve grown into a leading provider of used and new car financing across the country.

Our Engineering and Analytics Team Members utilize the latest technology to develop, monitor, and maintain complex practices that help optimize our success. Our Team Members value being challenged, are encouraged to express their ideas, and have the flexibility to enjoy work life balance. We build intrinsic value by partnering with all functions of our business to support their success and make strategic business decisions. We focus on professional development and continuous improvement while enjoying a casual work environment and Great Place to Work culture!

Credit Acceptance makes vehicle ownership possible for consumers other lenders decline, through a dealer network, an originations and servicing platform, and pricing and decisioning models refined over decades. The technology estate underneath this business was built project by project over a long period, and modernizing it is the largest engineering opportunity at the company. As the Distinguished Engineer, you are the senior-most individual contributor in Technology, reporting directly to the Chief Technology Officer. You will set the multi-year technical strategy for the company while staying close enough to the code and systems to remain credible — this is not an architect role that reviews designs from a distance, nor a strong engineer role that goes deep in a single domain. Two things sit at the center of the job: the target architecture for the enterprise, and the architecture for running AI agents across it. You will not own a team; you will own the hardest technical problems the company has, and get them resolved by convincing the people who do own the teams.

Outcomes and Activities

  • Enterprise target architecture: Convene the principal and staff engineers who own each domain to define the end-state architecture across originations, servicing, marketplace, data, and AI, and use it to drive the multi-year plan. Ensure every component has a defined interface with stated inputs and outputs, every unmade decision has a written principle standing in for it, and the document states honestly how close the organization is to the end state. Publish the architecture, including the tradeoffs that were rejected and why.
  • Agentic AI architecture across the enterprise: Own the enterprise agent architecture spanning servicing and collections, the dealer side, originations, and internal engineering and back-office workflows, built on one common foundation rather than one stack per team. Establish a governed way for agents to discover and call business capabilities, data, and tools, using the Model Context Protocol as the integration layer. Define an identity and authorization model that treats an agent as a first-class actor with its own least-privilege entitlements, along with observability, evaluation, and cost controls that work consistently for every agent. Set policy on what an agent may decide independently versus what stays with a person, and define where that line moves and on what evidence. Design the architecture to produce an examiner-ready record of what each agent saw, recommended, and touched, and set the evaluation and adversarial testing approach that makes agent outcomes defensible. Ensure the same foundation and controls apply to agents built by outside firms on the company's behalf.
  • Migration off on-premises infrastructure: Own the technical strategy for migrating transactional and analytical workloads off on-premises infrastructure to the company's strategic targets — AWS for transactional workloads and Databricks for analytical workloads — determining what lifts and shifts, what replatforms, what gets re-architected on the way versus after, and what the steady-state cost looks like. Own the resilience and recovery architecture for the target state.
  • Data platform architecture: Set the architecture for change-data-capture-based ingestion, streaming where warranted, and a modern warehouse with no job-scheduling dependency, moving the organization from largely batch analytical data movement to real time. Help settle the open question of who owns the transactional and analytical data models.
  • Real-time decisioning, model serving, and experimentation: Architect for pricing and credit model and scorecard updates that drop in as a layer rather than requiring a multi-quarter rebuild, and for an experimentation platform that supports orders of magnitude more concurrent experiments than a conventional release process allows.
  • Marketplace and search architecture: Own the architecture and interfaces for a unified vehicle inventory, consumer search, and lead routing platform, ensuring the data model supports more than one class of seller from the start.
  • AI-native engineering practice: Define the golden path for how software is specified, generated, reviewed, tested, and deployed, including the analyzers and gates that enforce it, and measure the inputs to that practice rather than just the outputs. Hold the build-versus-buy bar for AI capability, building what is core competency and about to scale, and renting the rest.
  • Performance and peak readiness: Own the instrumentation, baseline, and remediation architecture needed to meet the standard that no page takes more than one second. Own peak-event headroom, including understanding the limits of each system and maintaining tested degradation levers ahead of need.
  • Operating approach: Move the organization from project-shaped systems toward owned platforms with stated contracts. Document every component's inputs and outputs, and be ready to argue why closely coupled components should not be consolidated into one. Work toward a two-week requirement-to-production iteration bar, treating architecture that cannot be delivered incrementally as unfinished. Name what comes off the plan whenever a change in direction is requested. Make the call and own the outcome on architectural recommendations. Treat security, privacy, auditability, and regulatory obligation as design inputs from the start in this regulated environment.
  • Hands-on, not hands-off: This is not optional. Stay personally engaged in the technical work rather than directing it from a distance. Join design reviews, write proofs of concept, read code, and engage in incident analysis. This hands-on time does not replace the work the teams own, and it is not a fallback when delivery slips. Every engineer in the organization will read how you write, how you argue a design, how you handle being wrong, and how you treat engineers who disagree with you as the bar. Staff and principal engineers should be measurably better at this work for having worked with you.
  • Success measures: A published target architecture the domain owners agree with and that the annual and long-range plans are actually written against; an enterprise agent foundation that internal teams and partners build on, with access controls, evaluation, and audit records in place; a credible, dated, costed migration path off on-premises infrastructure and demonstrated progress against it; measured improvement in chosen input metrics such as latency, availability, recovery objectives, deployment frequency, and experiment throughput; growth in the number of principal and staff engineers who are better at this work as a result of this role; and architectural decisions that stop being relitigated because the reasoning was written down and the interfaces were clear.

Competencies

The following items detail how you will be successful in this role. At this level, you are expected to set the standard for each.

  • Customer Empathy: Customer Empathy is the ability to understand the perspectives, pain points, and experiences of customers. It involves actively putting oneself in the customer’s shoes, comprehending their needs and challenges, and using that understanding to provide a better, more customer-centric experience.
  • Engineering Excellence: Engineering Excellence is about bringing great craftsmanship and thought leadership to deliver an outstanding product that delights customers and solves for the business. This involves the pursuit and achievement of high standards, best practices, innovation, and superior solutions.
  • One Team: A One Team mindset refers to a collaborative approach across the organization, where individuals work together seamlessly, without boundaries, as a single, cohesive team. Shared goals, open communication and mutual support create a sense of collective purpose. This enables teams to navigate challenges and pursue shared objectives more effectively.
  • Owner’s Mindset: Owner’s Mindset involves adopting a set of behaviors that reflect a sense of responsibility, accountability, strategic thinking, and a proactive approach to managing your domain. As an owner, you understand the business and your domain(s) deeply and solve for the right outcome for the domain(s) and the business.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or closely related field of study; or equivalent work experience
  • Minimum 10 years of software engineering experience or comparable depth of experience
  • A track record of setting and delivering multi-year technical strategy at enterprise scale, as an individual contributor rather than through a reporting line.
  • Depth in distributed systems architecture, and in at least two of: agentic or LLM-based systems in production; large-scale cloud migration of transactional systems; modern data platform and lakehouse architecture; machine learning platform and model serving; high-traffic consumer or marketplace applications.
  • Architecture ownership of agentic or LLM-based systems that reached production, including how tool and data access were governed, how the system was evaluated, and what its failure modes turned out to be.
  • Demonstrated ownership of a legacy-to-modern migration of systems the business runs on, including the sequencing, the cost case, and the failure modes, with production revenue at stake rather than only familiarity with the concept.
  • Hands-on credibility today: actively reads code, writes proofs of concept, joins design reviews, and participates in incident analysis.
  • Evidence of influence without authority across organizational boundaries, including work that changed direction at the executive level.
  • Strong written communication; architecture here is carried by documents that other people can act on without the author in the room.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop staff and principal engineers, and to raise the technical bar of engineers not directly managed.
  • Experience delivering in a regulated industry, or a clear ability to work inside audit, security, and compliance constraints without treating them as an obstacle.

Preferred Experience

  • Recognized contribution beyond one employer, such as open source, standards work, publications, patents, or a sustained external technical presence.
  • Consumer lending, auto finance, insurance, or payments experience; or large-scale distributed systems experience supporting a business-critical function in another high-stakes domain.
  • The Model Context Protocol or comparable agent tool-integration standards, and identity and authorization design for non-human actors.
  • AWS and Databricks at production scale.
  • Experience standing up an experimentation platform, or moving an organization from tens to thousands of experiments per year.
  • Experience building AI-native development practice across a large engineering organization, and measuring whether it worked.
  • Marketplace, search, or inventory systems with more than one class of seller.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Distributed Systems Mastery: Technical mastery across distributed systems and software architecture, with deep knowledge of current and emerging technologies and their business implications.
  • Enterprise Problem-Solving: Ability to solve enterprise-wide problems where no precedent exists and to own cross-team shared infrastructure.
  • Strategic Independence: Ability to define and execute technical strategy for the entire organization, partner closely with executives, mobilize resources, and drive consensus across stakeholders at all levels.
  • Visionary Leadership: Bold strategic thinking paired with curiosity, ingenuity, and resourcefulness; recognized industry-level thought leadership and a commitment to lifelong learning.
  • Customer and Market Insight: Company-wide expertise in customer needs, using deep customer and market understanding to shape product and technical strategy and anticipate the impact of industry trends.
  • Technical Writing: Ability to produce architecture documentation clear and complete enough for others to act on independently.
  • Executive Communication and Influence: Ability to build consensus and influence direction across organizational and executive boundaries without formal authority.
  • Talent Development: Ability to raise the technical bar of engineers across the organization, including staff and principal engineers who are not direct reports.

Target Compensation: A competitive base salary range from $232,500 - $341,000. This position is eligible for equity and annual cash bonuses. Final compensation within the range is influenced by many factors including role-specific skills, depth and experience level, industry background, relevant education and certifications.

jobs.excerpt: Ready to embark on the quest of joining Hack The Box?
jobs.description:
Ready to embark on the quest of joining Hack The Box?

At the end of this thrilling journey, you'll become a proud member of Hack The Box, with the ultimate mission to help cybersecurity professionals and organizations enhance their cyber-attack readiness. Get ready for an exciting adventure into the world of cybersecurity! 🚀🔒💻

✨The core mission of the EMEA Field Marketing Manager:

This is an exciting opportunity to lead Hack The Box’s field marketing strategy across Europe, with a primary focus on the commercial and enterprise markets.

You will serve as the strategic marketing partner to the EMEA Sales organization, building integrated regional programs that generate demand, deepen engagement within priority accounts, accelerate opportunities, and contribute to pipeline and revenue.

This role is broader than event marketing. Events will be one component of a coordinated regional strategy that also includes account-based marketing, digital campaigns, webinars, executive programs, partner activation, customer marketing, content, and sales plays.

During your first six months, you will focus on developing the EMEA marketing strategy, building strong relationships with Sales, identifying regional priorities and target accounts, launching initial campaigns, and establishing a consistent approach to reporting and optimization.

🏢 Location & Work Mode:

  • Europe (EoR - Employee of Record through Deel) OR Athens, Greece (we'll support your relocation)
  • If in Athens, Greece: Hybrid (2 days in office)
  • Full time

✈️ Relocation

  • We offer a 10% relocation bonus on the annual salary to support your move.
  • In addition, you would benefit from a 50% tax reduction on your income as part of the relocation.
  • We'll support you with accommodation during the first few weeks

🍺 The fellowship you’ll be joining:

Reporting to the Global Director of Field Marketing, you will join Hack The Box’s global marketing organization and collaborate closely with Demand Generation, Partner Marketing, Product Marketing, Content, Digital, Brand, Communications, Customer Marketing, and Marketing Operations.

You will be a key partner to EMEA Sales leadership, account executives, business development representatives, solutions engineers, and channel teams. You will help connect global marketing priorities with the needs of the region and operate as the marketing lead for your market.

🚀 The adventures that await you after becoming an EMEA Field Marketing Manager

  • Own the EMEA field marketing strategy from ideation and planning through execution, measurement, and optimization.
  • Partner with EMEA Sales leadership to develop quarterly and annual marketing plans aligned with regional pipeline, revenue, and account goals.
  • Build integrated regional campaigns using account-based marketing, digital programs, content, webinars, executive engagement, partner initiatives, customer advocacy, and strategic events.
  • Translate global campaigns into relevant regional programs based on EMEA market needs, sales priorities, buyer challenges, and competitive trends.
  • Develop account-based programs for priority enterprise accounts and strategic opportunities.
  • Create marketing plays that help Sales open doors, engage additional buying-group members, progress opportunities, and re-engage stalled or closed-lost accounts.
  • Partner with Business Development and Sales to establish clear lead follow-up plans, campaign activation strategies, and shared success metrics.
  • Develop audience-specific programs for CISOs, security leaders, technical practitioners, talent-development leaders, and other members of the buying committee.
  • Build regional webinar, roundtable, executive-engagement, and thought-leadership programs that position Hack The Box as a leader in cyber workforce readiness.
  • Create coordinated pre-event, onsite, and post-event campaigns that extend the value of trade shows and field programs.
  • Work with Partner Marketing to develop joint campaigns that generate demand and pipeline with strategic channel and technology partners.
  • Collaborate with Customer Marketing to feature customer stories, support expansion opportunities, and build regional advocacy.
  • Manage the EMEA field marketing budget and make investment recommendations based on strategic importance and expected business impact.
  • Establish clear goals for every program, including target-account engagement, lead quality, pipeline creation, opportunity acceleration, and influenced revenue.
  • Communicate campaign plans, performance, insights, and next steps consistently to Sales and Marketing stakeholders.
  • Analyze results and sales feedback to improve audience targeting, messaging, channel selection, and future investments.
  • Maintain visibility into regional market trends, customer needs, competitor activity, and emerging opportunities.

What success looks like

  • A clear, scalable, and measurable EMEA field marketing strategy is in place.
  • Sales and Marketing are aligned around regional priorities, target accounts, programs, and goals.
  • Integrated campaigns create qualified pipeline and influence revenue.
  • Engagement increases within priority accounts and across key buying groups.
  • Marketing programs support both new-logo acquisition and opportunity acceleration.
  • Regional events operate as part of broader campaigns with measurable pre-event and post-event outcomes.
  • Program insights are consistently used to optimize the marketing mix and regional investment strategy.

🏆 Skills, knowledge, and experience points required to unlock the role of EMEA Field Marketing Manager:

  • At least five years of B2B marketing experience, including field marketing, demand generation, account-based marketing (ABM), or integrated campaigns.
  • Experience marketing enterprise SaaS or technology solutions; cybersecurity experience is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated success building regional, multi-channel marketing programs that contribute to pipeline generation, opportunity acceleration, and revenue growth.
  • Strong understanding of enterprise sales cycles, account-based marketing, buying groups, and opportunity acceleration, with a track record of working closely with Sales, Business Development, Partner, and Customer Success teams.
  • Hands-on experience with marketing automation, CRM, ABM, analytics, and reporting platforms such as HubSpot. Experience using AI-powered marketing tools to improve campaign planning, content development, audience targeting, personalization, and performance analysis is highly desirable.
  • Ability to develop marketing strategies aligned with business objectives while remaining hands-on in campaign execution. Strong project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple campaigns, stakeholders, budgets, and deadlines.
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder-management skills, with a creative, adaptable approach and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced global organization.

🕹️ What your Hack The Box adventure will have in store:

  • 🎯You'll have the exhilarating opportunity to contribute to a product that is highly appreciated by users and the cybersecurity community at large.
  • 🎯 You'll experience a highly supportive and caring environment, fostering growth, flexibility, and autonomy.
  • 🎯 You'll embark on an exciting journey of continuous learning and problem-solving, leveling up as our organization grows.
  • 🎯 Most importantly, you'll have a blast at HTB 🥳 because fun is an essential ingredient in our recipe for success! Just wait until you see our global meet-ups!

💰The gems you’ll be enjoying as an EMEA Field Marketing Manager:

  • Private Health Care & Life Insurance
  • Home Office Allowance
  • Ticket Restaurant Allowance
  • Paid paternity leave
  • Dedicated budget for training and professional development, participation in conferences
  • State-of-the-art equipment
  • Full access to the Hack The Box lab offerings; so you can learn how to hack 😉
  • Fully remote is an option. But we do have an office in London & Folkestone, UK

🗺️ The Quest of Becoming Hack The Box’s EMEA Field Marketing Manager:

  • Level 1 — Apply: Submit your application. Tell us why this role excites you and what you’d bring.
  • Level 2 — Talent Screen: A conversation with our Talent Acquisition team to explore your background and ambitions.
  • Level 3 — Chat with Jamie or Tom: A relaxed conversation with your future manager / department lead. Think of it as a mutual vibe check.
  • Level 4 — Complete a job-specific challenge and have a meaningful conversation with the team.
  • Level 5 — Congratulations! Not many reach this level 💪. Level’s objective: have a constructive, final conversation with senior leadership to explore the role and your future at HTB.
  • Level 6 — You've officially received an offer from HTB! To complete the last level and the Quest, all you need to do is accept the offer.
  • Quest complete. Congratulations, you’re officially one of us 🥳🎉🎇Your next quest: complete the onboarding.

Hack Your Career, Today. Join us in this epic adventure of cybersecurity at Hack The Box! 🚀🔒💻

At Hack The Box, we are on a quest to find the most exceptional and enthusiastic talent to join our team. Whether or not you consider yourself a gamer, we value what makes you unique and want to know more about you. This job post provides just a glimpse of the incredible gamified experience our business and consumer customers enjoy through our platforms. So, if you're ready to embark on a journey of disruption, growth, and adventure, we can't wait to meet you!

ABOUT HACK THE BOX

Job Title

Senior Director of Operations & Supply Chain (CPG)

Job Description

About the Position |Major goals and objectives and location requirements:

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on Senior Operations Director to build and lead end-to-end operations for a new CPG beverage brand. You will own the physical life cycle of the product—from commercialization and sourcing through production, inventory, warehousing, shipping, and replenishment. You’ll work closely with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and manufacturing partners to ensure we make the right product, at the right quality and cost, and get it where it needs to go on time. This is a role for a builder and operator—someone who can create scalable systems and partnerships while staying close enough to production and supply chain execution to solve problems quickly.


What You’ll Do

  • Own end-to-end operations from commercialization through production, customer delivery and replenishment.
  • Build the supply chain, vendor network and operating processes required to launch and scale the business.
  • Translate forecasts into production, inventory and supply plans, including co-manufacturer capacity, scheduling and production readiness.
  • Manage sourcing and external partners across ingredients, packaging, co-manufacturers, warehouses, 3PLs and freight.
  • Work closely with the VP/GM on the commercialization of new products and formats across formula, packaging, specifications and production requirements.
  • Partner with quality, regulatory and technical resources on food safety, process authority and compliance.
  • Own inventory, warehousing, fulfillment and transportation across retail, distributor, foodservice and DTC channels.
  • Own key components of COGS and landed cost, while managing operational KPIs across production, inventory, service, freight and cost.

What We’re Looking For

  • 10+ years of operations, supply chain or manufacturing experience, including at least 7 years in beverage.
  • Direct beverage manufacturing experience required, ideally in RTD, non-alcoholic beverages, beer, wine, or spirits utilizing glass and aluminum packaging.
  • Experience managing products from commercialization through production, distribution, and replenishment.
  • Strong experience with co-manufacturers/co-packers, outsourced manufacturing and external supply-chain partners.
  • Deep knowledge of production planning, sourcing, ingredients and packaging, inventory, warehousing and transportation.
  • Strong financial and operational judgment, including COGS, landed cost, budgets, working capital, vendor negotiation and project management.
  • A builder mentality with the ability to move quickly between strategy and hands-on execution in a fast-moving environment where the operating infrastructure is being built rapidly.

Remote

jobs.description:
About Nerdio

At Nerdio, our mission is to simplify the lives of IT professionals and maximize their Microsoft cloud and end user computing investments.

We support organizations of all sizes looking to deploy, manage, and cost-optimize native Microsoft technologies. We partner with Enterprises and Managed Service Providers all over the world to add value on top of their existing native Microsoft investments like Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), Windows 365, and Microsoft Intune.

Created in 2016, Nerdio has always taken a market-leading and collaborative approach to cloud deployment and management. In fact, our product roadmap is greatly influenced by the regular feedback we receive from having seen companies deploy AVD into production environments several thousand times using Nerdio technology.

Today, Nerdio is used in over 50 countries by more than 15,000 organizations of every size and vertical. We’re committed to delivering exceptional service and support, which starts with identifying and supporting the best staff possible.

We are a fast-moving, nimble company looking for individuals who are collaborative, empathetic, driven and who love to move at the speed of light. If you want to be part of the AVD transformation that Microsoft and Nerdio are leading, then we want to speak with you.

About the role

As a Senior Recruiter at Nerdio, you will be a strategic talent partner to leaders across EMEA and APAC, helping us hire the people who will drive our next phase of growth. Working 100% remotely from the UK as part of our global Talent Acquisition team, you will own full life cycle recruiting for every line of business in the region, from senior leadership, sales and sales engineering to product, technical support, marketing and beyond.

You will build trusted relationships with hiring managers and key stakeholders, act as their go-to advisor on talent strategy and local market dynamics, and build proactive talent pipelines so we are ready for the roles of tomorrow, not just the roles open today. This is a full-time role for an experienced recruiter who thrives in fast-paced tech environments, brings excellent sourcing skills and strong communication, and enjoys working across cultures and time zones. You will represent the Nerdio brand, culture and values throughout the hiring process.

What you’ll do

  • Own full life cycle recruiting across EMEA and APAC for all lines of business, including leadership, sales, sales engineering, product, technical support, marketing and other functions, from intake through to offer and onboarding handover.
  • Act as a strategic Talent Acquisition advisor to hiring managers and senior leaders: shape hiring plans, define role requirements, and advise on market insights, compensation benchmarks, recruiting best practices and realistic timelines.
  • Build a deep understanding of the EMEA and APAC talent markets, including talent supply, salary expectations, local hiring practices and language needs, and turn that insight into tailored, country-specific search strategies.
  • Build and nurture proactive talent pipelines for current and future roles, engaging passive candidates, talent communities, networks and referrals well ahead of demand.
  • Lead creative, high-quality sourcing using LinkedIn Recruiter, advanced Boolean and market mapping, direct outreach, events, communities and referral programs.
  • Screen candidates for skills, experience and alignment with Nerdio’s culture and mission, and partner with hiring teams to run structured, consistent and inclusive interview processes.
  • Coordinate interviews, gather and share feedback, and guide hiring teams through evaluation and decision-making.
  • Deliver an outstanding candidate experience from first outreach to offer and beyond, and manage offers and negotiations in partnership with the People team, in line with local requirements.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date candidate records in the ATS, and share pipeline health, funnel metrics and hiring progress with stakeholders.
  • Continuously improve our recruiting processes, tools and documentation, share best practices, and collaborate with Talent Acquisition and People colleagues across regions, including the US.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in human resources, business administration or a related field is preferred.
  • 7+ years of full life cycle recruiting experience, including at least 3 years in-house in a tech or SaaS environment.
  • Proven experience recruiting across multiple functions, including go-to-market (sales, sales engineering, marketing), technical support and product. Experience hiring senior leaders is a strong plus.
  • Demonstrated success recruiting across EMEA and/or APAC, with a solid understanding of regional talent markets, hiring practices and cultural differences.
  • Excellent sourcing skills and a track record of building proactive talent pipelines for hard-to-fill and passive talent.
  • Ability to build strong relationships with hiring managers and senior stakeholders and to act as a trusted, strategic Talent Acquisition advisor.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and manage expectations across cultures and time zones.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple searches at once and handle confidential information with discretion.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and HR software (e.g. HRIS, ATS)
  • (Plus) Experience recruiting for roles related to:
    • Cloud computing / Azure / Microsoft ecosystem
    • Sales engineering or technical support
    • Go-to-market teams in SaaS
  • (Plus) Fluency in an additional EMEA or APAC language.
  • Adaptability, a proactive attitude and strong problem-solving skills in a fast-paced environment.
  • Based in the UK with the right to work in the UK, and flexibility to work across time zones to support colleagues in EMEA, APAC and the US.

jobs.description:
1099 Contractor Opportunity

Cybersecurity Internal Auditor (ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001)

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Cybersecurity Internal Audit Consultant (1099 Contractor) to perform independent internal audits of information security, privacy, and AI management systems. The consultant will be responsible for assessing organizational compliance against multiple management system standards, identifying gaps, evaluating control effectiveness, and providing actionable recommendations to support certification readiness and continual improvement.

This role is ideal for an experienced auditor who has performed internal audits for organizations pursuing or maintaining certifications such as ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001, and related cybersecurity and compliance frameworks.

Engagement Type

  • Independent Contractor (1099)
  • Remote with occasional virtual meetings
  • Project-based with opportunity for recurring engagements
  • Flexible scheduling based on audit plans and certification timelines

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan and execute internal audits against:
    • ISO/IEC 27001 Information Security Management Systems (ISMS)
    • ISO/IEC 27701 Privacy Information Management Systems (PIMS)
    • ISO/IEC 42001 Artificial Intelligence Management Systems (AIMS)
    • Additional standards and frameworks as applicable
  • Review policies, procedures, standards, risk assessments, and supporting documentation.
  • Assess operational effectiveness of security, privacy, and AI governance controls.
  • Conduct interviews with stakeholders, control owners, and process owners.
  • Validate evidence supporting compliance requirements.
  • Identify nonconformities, observations, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Develop detailed audit reports, findings, and corrective action recommendations.
  • Present audit results to leadership and management teams.
  • Assist with remediation validation and follow-up assessments.
  • Provide guidance on audit preparedness and continual improvement activities.

Required Qualifications

  • ISO 27001 Lead Auditor certification.
  • ISO 27701 auditing experience.
  • ISO 42001 auditing experience.
  • Experience conducting cybersecurity, privacy, risk, or compliance audits.
  • Demonstrated experience auditing against ISO management system standards.
  • Strong understanding of:
    • Information Security Governance
    • Risk Management
    • Access Control
    • Incident Response
    • Vendor Risk Management
    • Privacy Programs
    • AI Governance and Risk Management
  • Experience interviewing stakeholders and evaluating control effectiveness.
  • Excellent report writing, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple audit engagements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA).
  • Certified Information Security Manager (CISM).
  • Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP).
  • Certified Internal Auditor (CIA).
  • Experience supporting accredited certification audits.
  • Knowledge of NIST CSF, NIST AI RMF, SOC 2, HITRUST, PCI DSS, or similar frameworks.

Compensation

  • Hourly or fixed-fee engagement depending on scope and experience.
  • Competitive market rates commensurate with certifications and relevant audit experience.

About DigniFi:
DigniFi’s Point-of-Sale financing solution helps 2,000+ partners increase revenue, drive accessory orders, and decrease deferred repairs. We partner with dealerships and service centers to offer financing products at the point of sale for auto repairs, service, parts, accessories, maintenance packages, and more.

As DigniFi continues to grow, our success depends on deep integrations with the software platforms dealerships already use every day. This role sits at the center of that strategy.
Our mission is to help auto dealers and service centers grow by offering their customers innovative, inclusive financing. Our vision is to make financing for the needs of daily life accessible and inclusive.

About The Role:

This executive will oversee financial planning and reporting, capital markets, fundraising, and securitization while building strong relationships with investors, lenders, and financing partners. jobs.description:
Fourth is the world’s largest and fastest-growing global leader of end-to-end restaurant and hospitality management technology solutions. We pride ourselves on delivering a world-class SaaS experience for our clients by building long-term partnerships starting from the first phone call. We know our recipe for success at Fourth is our amazing team... and that starts with hiring the right people!

Interested in joining our smart, fun, and talented team?

Position Overview

  • HotSchedules is the restaurant industry’s most widely used scheduling platform. Over 300,000 restaurants across North America trust HotSchedules. The SMB team is at the top of our growth funnel—introducing restaurant operators to HotSchedules.

  • As the dedicated demand gen marketer for SMB, you’ll own the pipeline programs that fuel bookings for two high-performing sales teams. Running both inbound programs and outbound sales-led campaigns to hit quarterly bookings targets.

  • Some of this GTM motion exists and needs refinement. Some of it you’ll create from scratch. You'll pull in Product Marketing, Sales, and RevOps when you need them — but you won't wait for alignment to move. You drive the work and bring people along.

  • The challenge in marketing today, the channels are crowded. The job is to find where there’s still signal, test aggressively, and scale what works. Plus, cutting what doesn’t work before it becomes a habit. That means bringing new ideas, tinkering with tools, and being willing to experiment your way to an answer. It also means knowing your customer deeply enough that your messaging cuts through. Understanding what operators care about, where they spend their time, and what makes them stop and listen.

Primary Responsibilities

Own pipeline:

  • Drive inbound and outbound demand programs end-to-end — strategy, execution, iteration — with a clear line to SAO targets each quarter. Pipeline and bookings are how we keep score.

Embed with sales:

  • Standups, call shadows, deal reviews. Short deal cycles mean fast feedback loops — you’ll know quickly what’s working and can act on it fast.

Build campaigns that earn attention:

  • Develop integrated, multi-touch programs across email, paid, content, and outbound that speak to operators’ reality.

Know your buyer:

  • Learn from regular operator interviews and sales calls to craft messaging, creative, and campaign strategy that works.

Build and evolve the stack:

  • Identify gaps, propose solutions, implement what works. You don’t wait for a better workflow — you build it.

Use AI to scale yourself:

  • Tools, workflows, agents. Use technology extends your capabilities and gain leverage.

Close the loop:

  • Partner with RevOps on scoring, routing, response times, and reporting.

Key Skills and Competencies

  • 5–7 years in B2B demand generation, ideally SaaS, with a track record of owning a pipeline number.

  • Fluent across channels: email, paid, content, events, outbound. Good enough at all of them to know which one to reach for and to connect them into programs that convert.

  • A strong writer who can speak to a small business owner’s daily reality.

  • Someone who embeds with sales rather than operating at arm’s length. Low ego, high output.

  • A tinkerer. You’ve built workflows, tested tools, played with agents — and you have real examples to show for it.

  • Comfortable being accountable. You track pipeline/ SAO targets like it's your own money. When the pipeline is short, you figure out why and fix it.

  • You've pulled your own pipeline and conversion data, found the problem before someone told you about it, and changed your program because of what you saw.

  • You've killed your own programs when the data said so — even ones you built and liked.

  • A curious, life-long learner

Why This Role

  • Restaurant operators run some of the hardest businesses in the world. When HotSchedules works, it makes their lives meaningfully easier. This role puts you at the front of that pipeline—it's how you get there, but the operator on the other end is why it matters.

Fourth Benefits

🏖 Unlimited PTO!

🏥 Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance!

🏦 401k Match!

👥 Parental Leave

💻 Laptop and equipment.

Remote employment limited to: AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, ID, IL, IN, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MN, MS, NC, NE, NJ, NM, NV, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, & WA


Our Story

In July 2019, Fourth joined forces with HotSchedules to become the global leader in end-to-end restaurant and hospitality management technology solutions. Together, the merged company now represents the world’s largest and only provider of end-to-end restaurant and hospitality management solutions for customers across the globe and of all sizes—from a single location or franchisee restaurant to a global restaurant or hotel chain. The combined company’s complete software-as-service (SaaS) solution suite, including scheduling, time & attendance, applicant tracking, training, inventory management/procurement, HR/benefits, and payroll services, now serves customers in 120,000 locations worldwide and is supported by a dedicated, unified team across offices in the US, UK, Bulgaria, China, Australia, and UAE.

Fourth is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.excerpt: Member Access Processing (MAP) is a trusted leader in payment processing solutions.
jobs.description:
Member Access Processing (MAP) is a trusted leader in payment processing solutions. We provide secure, efficient, and tailored services to financial institutions and businesses, enabling seamless transactions for their customers. With a focus on innovation, reliability, and customer satisfaction, MAP is committed to delivering cutting-edge technology and exceptional service in the ever-evolving world of payments. We pride ourselves on creating a positive, collaborative work environment where our employees can grow and make a meaningful impact.

Overview

The Product Enablement Lead is responsible for designing, developing, maintaining, and delivering product learning experiences that help credit unions and MAP employees confidently adopt, use, and optimize MAP products and supporting Visa DPS platforms. This role owns the product enablement content lifecycle, from evaluating the learning impact of new products and enhancements through curriculum development, delivery, measurement, and ongoing content maintenance.

The ideal candidate combines practical credit and debit card processing experience with knowledge of fraud and dispute operations, credit union core environments, instructional design, and adult learning. The role translates complex product and operational information into clear, practical, hands-on learning experiences that support client readiness, product adoption, operational consistency, and a strong client experience.

This role helps shift MAP’s learning model from presentation-based training to experiential enablement focused on system proficiency, workflow execution, troubleshooting, decision-making, and operational readiness. Success is measured not only by training delivery, but by whether learners can confidently perform the work, navigate applicable systems, troubleshoot common scenarios, and apply their knowledge after training.

Role and Responsibilities

Product & Systems Expertise

  • Maintain current, working knowledge of MAP products and services, including MAP Defense, MAP Data, card processing solutions, Visa DPS systems, and related operational tools.
  • Monitor the Visa DPS product roadmap, release communications, product enhancements, and changes to existing products to determine training and enablement impacts.
  • Partner with internal subject matter experts and Visa DPS resources to validate product information, workflows, dependencies, and client-facing guidance before training content is released.
  • Understand how MAP and Visa DPS products interact with credit union core systems and processing environments and translate those differences into practical training guidance.
  • Conduct ongoing research across MAP, Visa, and Visa DPS documentation to keep learning materials accurate, relevant, and current.
  • Maintain practical knowledge of end-to-end credit and debit card processing, including authorization, clearing and settlement, transaction lifecycle, disputes, fraud, card servicing, transaction controls, and common exception scenarios.
  • Develop working proficiency within relevant processor tools and environments sufficient to demonstrate workflows, recreate common scenarios, and guide learners through system-based exercises.
  • Understand the relationship between issuer configuration, processor functionality, network requirements, core systems, and downstream operational impacts.
  • Maintain knowledge of common payment terminology, transaction flows, response codes, authorization behavior, and processing concepts necessary to effectively train and support MAP employees and clients.
  • Partner with operational subject matter experts to understand recurring support issues and incorporate those scenarios into training and reinforcement materials.

Curriculum & Content Development

  • Develop role-based learning paths, instructor-led programs, virtual learning, tutorials, workflow guides, playbooks, job aids, knowledge articles, videos, assessments, and Membership.io learning hub content.
  • Create complete product enablement packages for new product launches and material enhancements, including facilitator guides, participant materials, demonstrations, exercises, practice scenarios, knowledge checks, and post-training resources.
  • Establish and maintain a curriculum roadmap that aligns planned training development with the Visa DPS roadmap, MAP product priorities, release timing, client readiness needs, and required content refresh cycles.
  • Customize training content to reflect different client processing environments, core-system considerations, operational workflows, user roles, and levels of product maturity.

jobs.excerpt: Who we areSamsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara’s Customer Education is looking for a creative Senior Instructional Designer. You’ll be part of an energetic team that will play a key role in Samsara’s growth and our customers’ long-term success. Opportunities and challenges include developing learning strategies to support our key customer personas and industries, innovating in AI-driven instructional development, contributing new ways for us to scale our process and our reach, and being a thought leader across Samsara. Learn more below!

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: The training you build helps customers use Samsara to keep drivers safe, get goods delivered on time, and keep critical operations running. When your content works, customers adopt faster, see value sooner, and keep their people safer on the road and on the job.
  • You thrive on turning complexity into clarity: Our product is expanding quickly, and our customers range from fleet managers to frontline drivers to executives. You’ll take technical, fast-changing features and turn them into learning experiences that are clear, engaging, and effective for each audience.
  • You’re a natural collaborator: You’ll partner with Customer Success, Product, Sales, and Implementation teams to understand what customers struggle with and build content that closes the gap. You’ll also work closely with a program manager who prioritizes the team’s quarterly roadmap, and you’re comfortable juggling multiple projects at once.
  • You’re excited about how learning is built now: You like to experiment with new tools, AI-assisted authoring, and faster development models, and you’re energized by iterating quickly rather than perfecting slowly. You’ll help shape how our team scales content across on-demand courses, video, in-app learning, live sessions, and certifications.
  • You are the architect of your own career: Our Customer Education team is still shaping its future, so you’ll have real autonomy and ownership. You’ll own the learning journey for a product area, starting with Safety, and can grow as the team and product portfolio grow.

In this role, you will:

  • Work with stakeholders across the company to define training requirements, learning goals and user needs for both customers and partners
  • Craft and build learning & credentialing experiences in different formats (online learning, audio, video, in-app, etc.), working within the constraints of different templates and business requirements
  • Leverage a wide range of tools (AI-based content authoring, multimedia) to develop content rapidly and iteratively
  • Push yourself and the team to evolve and improve upon our processes, and to discover and test new instructional development models and tooling
  • Solicit reviews from partners and SMEs, and review others’ content and assessments for effectiveness
  • Own an assigned Samsara product area, by monitoring updates, maintaining its curriculum, and partnering with leadership on incoming requests
  • Build product expertise through self-directed research, available AI tools, and targeted collaboration with SMEs to validate content
  • Design and write engaging and effective assessments
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s values and operating principles as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 3-5+ years learning design or instructional design experience in a software/Saas setting
  • Knowledge of Instructional Design standard methodologies and a proven ability to craft learning content that is effective and engaging
  • Ability to communicate abstract or technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences (visually and in writing)
  • Ability to identify the best learning delivery formats (e.g., online learning, assessments, audio-based lessons) for a specific set of objectives
  • Collaboration skills and teamwork
  • Attention to design aesthetics and visual detail.
  • Knowledge of legacy and emerging content development tools such as: , Articulate, Camtasia, Zoom, Clueso etc.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Comfort working within an AI-driven content development process, including AI-assisted authoring, review, and iteration
  • Experience developing in-app training or contextual product education

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$76,457.50—$115,650 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

jobs.excerpt: We are excited to speak to you about this opportunity.
jobs.description:
We are excited to speak to you about this opportunity. If you are interested in joining our growing team, please apply to this link directly.

Who we are

At Aquila, we invest in category-defining B2B/B2G software companies globally, acting as a thought-partner, striving for the success of our companies in the long term. We are a well-managed, profitable company that operates like a startup with the financial backing of a parent company. For our people, this means limitless possibilities.

We are unapologetically unique, pivoting to respond to the needs of the multiple markets we operate in. We have ambitious goals, and we are looking for genuine contributors with integrity, energy, flexibility, and loyalty. We are investing in building future leaders who can take an idea and make things happen.

At Emphasys HFA (Housing Finance Agency), a division of Emphasys, we build and support the only end-to-end financial software in the U.S. dedicated to affordable housing. As the largest full-service provider in this space, we enable State Housing Finance Agencies and other public organizations to administer programs that help families access affordable homeownership or rental housing. Our solutions power the financial backbone that processes funding, manages compliance, and ensures every dollar of support is tracked and maximized.

Who we need

Reporting to the Strategic Account Executive, we are hiring a Business Development Representative to support Emphasys HFA's growth and expand the capacity of our sales function. As our new Business Development Representative, you will combine targeted business development with hands-on support across RFPs, contracts, customer opportunities, and the early stages of the sales process. You will research the HFA market, identify new contacts and opportunities across existing and prospective accounts, coordinate information across Product, Client Services, Marketing, and other teams, and help move opportunities forward. Over time, as you build your knowledge and confidence, you will have the opportunity to take ownership of smaller product sales opportunities from initial conversation through close.

This is a full-time, remote role based in the United States. Eastern or Central Time zones are preferred.

What’s in it for you

Purpose and impact. You will represent technology that supports Housing Finance Agencies and public organizations delivering affordable homeownership and rental housing programs. Your work will help connect these organizations with the software they rely on to manage the financial and operational backbone of their programs, giving you a clear connection between the relationships you build, the solutions you introduce, and the communities those organizations serve.

A foundation for a long-term sales career. You will gain experience well beyond prospecting, working alongside experienced Sales, Marketing, Client Services, and Product teams and gaining exposure to customer relationships, RFPs, contracts, cross-sell opportunities, and the full sales cycle. As you build your knowledge and demonstrate your ability to manage opportunities, you will have the opportunity to take ownership of smaller product sales from start to close and continue expanding your responsibilities. As part of Constellation Software, you will also be joining a broader organization with opportunities to grow your career over time.

Specialized expertise in an evolving technology market. Emphasys has an established presence in a highly specialized market, with relationships across Housing Finance Agencies and multiple solutions that create opportunities to deepen and expand customer partnerships. You will build valuable expertise in affordable housing technology and public-sector sales while working for a business that is becoming increasingly AI-forward, giving you the opportunity to use modern tools in your research and sales work and learn how emerging technology can support customers and shape the market.

How you will make an impact

  • Create new opportunities. You will research the HFA market, identify prospective contacts and untapped opportunities, and use targeted outreach to create meaningful conversations. You will also work with existing customer relationships to identify opportunities to introduce additional Emphasys HFA products to teams and departments that may not currently use them.
  • Move opportunities forward. You will qualify interest, understand customer needs, identify the right stakeholders, and connect opportunities with the Strategic Account Executive when they are ready for deeper sales engagement. You will nurture relationships with longer timelines and continue building knowledge until an opportunity is ready to progress.
  • Coordinate RFP responses. You will help identify relevant RFP opportunities and coordinate the information needed to respond. You will work with Product Managers and other internal teams to gather answers, build response matrices, organize documentation, and keep the process moving through detailed and complex government procurement requirements.
  • Support contracts and customer opportunities. You will help organize contract documentation and follow up on items such as insurance certificates and other required materials. You will support the process without owning pricing or final commercial decisions, ensuring the right information is gathered and the opportunity continues moving toward completion.
  • Take ownership of smaller opportunities. As you build your product knowledge and demonstrate your ability to manage the process, you will have the opportunity to take smaller, lower-value product opportunities from initial conversation through close. This will give you hands-on experience managing the full sales cycle and building confidence as a technology sales professional.
  • Bring market insight back to the team. You will listen carefully to prospects and customers, stay curious about changing HFA needs, and share what you are learning with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Client Services. Your observations will help the team understand where opportunities exist and how Emphasys can better engage the market.
  • Use technology to work smarter. You will use CRM, LinkedIn, sales and research tools, and AI-enabled technology to research accounts, organize information, prepare outreach, and work more efficiently. You will look for practical ways technology can improve your approach to business development.

You bring

  • The sales foundation. You have experience in business development, sales development, lead generation, inside sales, account development, or a related customer-facing role. You may also be earlier in your sales career with other professional experience that demonstrates your interest in building a career in technology sales.
  • The curiosity and critical thinking. You ask thoughtful questions, listen carefully, and genuinely want to understand how a customer operates before deciding how to engage them. You can look at a complex situation, identify what needs to happen next, and work through the steps rather than stopping at the first obstacle.
  • The drive. You are comfortable creating opportunities rather than waiting for them to appear. You can handle unanswered outreach and rejection without losing momentum, while staying persistent, professional, and thoughtful in your follow-up.
  • The organization. You can manage multiple opportunities, follow up with different stakeholders, keep documentation accurate, and stay on top of details. You are comfortable coordinating information across teams and know that moving an opportunity forward often requires persistence and follow-through.
  • The communication and collaboration. You can build rapport with different types of stakeholders and communicate clearly in writing and conversation. You enjoy working with Product, Client Services, Marketing, and Sales rather than operating independently, and you know how to seek out the right person when you need information or support.
  • The technology mindset. You are comfortable learning new technology and interested in using AI and digital tools to improve how you research, communicate, and work. Experience with CRM, LinkedIn, sales engagement platforms, or software sales is an asset.
  • The market knowledge. Experience in housing, affordable housing, Housing Finance Agencies, government, or technology is an asset. We are also open to someone with strong sales potential who wants to develop expertise in this specialized market.

Join us.

As an Aquila company, Emphasys Software brings together bright, talented people who aspire to excellence and share a commitment to upholding our mission: To be a company of outstanding people delivering vertical market software solutions through long-term partnerships with clients.

Our entrepreneurial culture, lean environment, and people come together to form a dynamic organization where purpose drives our growth. With the autonomy to be creative and curious, we collaborate and iterate to achieve real impact in the communities we support.

Apply now.

Diversity and inclusion are not mere words on paper to us. We welcome and appreciate candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences. If you have 70% of the qualifications we are looking for and want to play an integral role in changing an industry, apply to express your interest.

What you can expect from our interview process:

  • A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor discussing your interest in the role, the team’s culture and your experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
  • A virtual interview with the Hiring Manager focused on your sales experience, approach to business development, curiosity, and ability to work through complex opportunities.
  • A final virtual interview with the General Manager, focused on your approach to collaboration, growth, and the opportunity to contribute to the sales function.

Aquila and Emphasys Software promote equal employment opportunities for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, national origin, veteran status, marital status or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities and accommodations are available on request.

Workday Technical Consultant - Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)
Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $100,000–$150,000 Annually
Experience Required: 6+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary
We are seeking a Workday Technical Consultant with broad expertise across Workday configuration, reporting, calculated fields, business process design, and Workday Extend application development. The role spans technical configuration, custom report design, integration support, and lightweight application extension work, helping HR, finance, and IT stakeholders get more value from the Workday platform. The ideal candidate combines strong Workday platform knowledge with practical engineering discipline and the ability to translate business requirements into clean, maintainable Workday configurations. In this role you will work closely with cross-functional partners — product, design, engineering, operations, and business stakeholders — to translate ambiguous requirements into well-engineered solutions, and will be expected to raise the bar through code review, design review, and mentorship of more junior engineers. Position: Supply Chain SpecialistSalary: up to $4,450 NZD per month – Depending on experience
Working Hours & Conditions: Full-time, remote position working New Zealand business hours
Holidays: TBC – Client Discretion

About the Business

The Business is dedicated to inspiring creators of great design and enabling exceptional interior spaces across Australia and New Zealand.

The company searches globally for leading trends, premium materials, hardware, surfaces and specialist expertise. These products are carefully curated for developers, architects, interior designers and other design professionals delivering high-quality projects.

As Architectural Merchants, it focuses on international quality standards, design excellence and reliable service, providing an exciting environment for professionals passionate about design-led products and supply chains.

Role Overview

We are seeking a capable and detail-oriented Supply Chain Specialist to coordinate the end-to-end supply chain activities supporting the company's curated product portfolio.

The successful candidate will manage inventory levels, coordinate procurement and replenishment, track international and domestic shipments, and ensure products are available to meet customer and project requirements.

This role requires close collaboration with suppliers, logistics providers and internal teams. The Supply Chain Specialist will also maintain accurate ERP records, monitor supply chain performance and identify opportunities to improve cost, efficiency and service delivery.

The key objective is to ensure the company’s products move through the supply chain reliably, accurately and cost-effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Inventory Planning & Replenishment

  • Monitor inventory levels across the company’s product portfolio.
  • Coordinate replenishment activities to maintain appropriate stock availability.
  • Review demand, current stock, committed orders and expected deliveries when planning purchases.
  • Identify potential stock shortages, excess inventory and slow-moving products.
  • Maintain appropriate reorder points, safety-stock levels and replenishment settings.
  • Work with sales, customer service and project teams to understand upcoming demand.
  • Support stocktakes, inventory reconciliations and the investigation of stock discrepancies.
  • Provide clear updates regarding product availability and expected delivery dates.

Procurement & Supplier Coordination

  • Prepare and manage purchase orders in accordance with approved requirements.
  • Liaise with local and international suppliers regarding pricing, availability, production and delivery schedules.
  • Confirm order quantities, specifications, costs and expected dispatch dates.
  • Monitor outstanding purchase orders and proactively follow up delayed or incomplete orders.
  • Maintain accurate supplier, product and purchasing information in the ERP system.
  • Communicate supply risks, pricing changes and delays to relevant internal stakeholders.
  • Develop positive and professional relationships with suppliers.
  • Support supplier-performance reviews and sourcing activities where required.

Logistics & Shipment Management

  • Coordinate and track inbound shipments from suppliers through to delivery.
  • Liaise with freight forwarders, transport providers, warehouses and other logistics partners.
  • Monitor shipping schedules, transit times and expected arrival dates.
  • Maintain accurate shipment records and supporting documentation.
  • Assist with basic import and export documentation and processes.
  • Identify potential delays or disruptions and communicate their likely impact.
  • Follow up damaged, incomplete, delayed or incorrectly supplied orders.
  • Support efficient and cost-effective freight and distribution decisions.

ERP, Data & Record Management

  • Maintain accurate product, supplier, inventory, purchase-order and shipment information in the ERP system.
  • Use NetSuite or Orcale ERP platform to manage and monitor supply chain activity.
  • Ensure records are updated promptly and consistently.
  • Review system data for errors, duplicate records and incomplete information.
  • Maintain accurate supporting documents for purchasing, inventory and logistics transactions.
  • Produce operational reports and data extracts as required.
  • Help improve data quality and consistency across supply chain systems.

Supply Chain Reporting & Analysis

  • Monitor supply chain metrics including inventory availability, order fulfilment, lead times, supplier performance and freight costs.
  • Prepare regular reports for management and relevant internal teams.
  • Analyse inventory and operational data to identify trends, risks and opportunities.
  • Investigate recurring delays, stock discrepancies and process inefficiencies.
  • Provide practical recommendations to improve supply chain performance.
  • Track agreed improvements and report on their outcomes.
  • Support forecasting, purchasing and operational planning with accurate data.

Internal Collaboration & Customer Support

  • Work closely with sales, customer service, finance, warehouse and project teams.
  • Provide accurate information regarding inventory availability, incoming stock and delivery expectations.
  • Support the resolution of supply chain issues affecting customers or projects.
  • Communicate clearly when timelines, availability or costs change.
  • Coordinate priorities where multiple customer or project requirements are competing for available stock.
  • Maintain professional communication with all internal and external stakeholders.

Process Improvement

  • Review existing procurement, inventory and logistics workflows.
  • Identify opportunities to improve accuracy, visibility, efficiency and cost control.
  • Help develop and document supply chain procedures, templates and checklists.
  • Support improvements to ERP processes and system usage.
  • Contribute to projects designed to strengthen inventory planning and supplier performance.
  • Apply a continuous-improvement mindset to day-to-day activities.

Tools & Systems

  • NetSuite / Oracle ERP – strong previous experience necessary
  • Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets
  • Purchasing and inventory-planning tools
  • Freight, logistics and shipment-tracking platforms
  • Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace
  • Reporting and data-analysis tools

Requirements

Key Requirements

  • At least three years of relevant supply chain, procurement, inventory or logistics experience.
  • Strong supply chain and inventory-management capability.
  • Experience coordinating purchasing, replenishment and stock availability.
  • Experience working with suppliers and logistics providers.
  • Practical experience using an ERP or inventory-management system.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets skills.
  • Ability to interpret operational data and monitor relevant KPIs.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and data accuracy.
  • Strong written and spoken English.
  • Professional communication skills when working with suppliers, logistics partners and internal teams.
  • Ability to manage multiple orders, shipments, priorities and deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently and take ownership of assigned responsibilities.
  • Comfortable working remotely and communicating regularly with the client.
  • Reliable internet connection and a professional home-office environment.
  • Availability to work full-time during New Zealand business hours.

Qualifications

  • A degree or diploma in supply chain management, logistics, operations, business or a related discipline would be advantageous.
  • Equivalent practical experience in a relevant supply chain role may be considered.

Highly Desirable

  • Hands-on experience using NetSuite.
  • Experience managing inventory for a wholesale, distribution, architectural-products or design-led business.
  • Experience working with internationally sourced products and overseas suppliers.
  • Understanding of import and export processes, shipping documentation and international freight.
  • Experience monitoring supplier performance, lead times and stock availability.
  • Exposure to demand planning, forecasting and inventory optimisation.
  • Experience supporting customers or projects with deadline-driven product requirements.
  • An interest in architecture, interior design, premium materials or design-led products.
